text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele accepted the resignation of Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss. Shkele said he would assume the duties of the minister until next year's budget is approved in parliament. The Democratic Party Saimnieks also said it would name candidates for the finance job after the budget was approved.

- In a telephone conversation with Shkele, Lithuania's prime minister, Mindaugas Stankevicius, put forward some new ideas on the border dispute between Latvia and Lithuania. Latvian foreign ministry state secretary Maris Riekstinsh said the Lithuanian ideas were actually only modified proposals of the Latvian side, expressed at the last round of negotiations.
- The vice-president of the Bank of Latvia Ilmar Rimshevich said the bank has finished working out the draft law which regulates insurance of deposits in commercial banks.

- The second round of border talks with Russia ended without any perceptible progress. Latvia insists Russia should pay compensation to people who lost their properties in the district Abrene-Pytalovo but Russia says it will not.

- On October 5-6, Riga will host the 9th session of the Baltic Assembly which is to formulate the position of the Baltic States regarding NATO admission. Arnold Ruutel, parliament vice-chairman, has submitted a document envisaging the formation of a joint military unit of the three Baltic States.
- Shkele said the financing of the army can only be increased if it comes at the expense of other ministries' budgets.
- The 1997 state budget will be considered and hopefully passed at the first reading on October 7.
- Minister of Defence Andrej Krastinsh said the Baltic Battallion will be transformed into a brigade to secure the rotation of its personnel.

- Members of the parliament committee for economic, agricultural, environmental and regional policy held a visiting session at the distillery Latvia's Balsams and tasted its production of alcoholic beverages.
